newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer shares drop on shift to bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Bayer shares drop on shift to bank shares.

text.p: Shares in German drugs and chemicals group Bayer AG on Thursday fell 2.3 percent in bourse trade as investors were said to be shifting funds into German bank shares.
Bayer shares dropped 1.37 marks to 57.18, outpacing losses at its rivals Hoechst AG and BASF AG and the 0.18 percent drop in the broader DAX index.
"People need money to buy the banks," said one dealer explaining Bayer's drop.

Another dealer added that Bayer, the maker of Bayer aspirin, was coming under pressure as French group Sanofi may soon launch a new drug that will be more effective than aspirin for use with heart patients.
Sanofi shares opened trading up 2.1 percent which traders said was due to the new drug.
